answer: Score identities by their failures, not their successes. A violet fable of flawless agents is cheap to script, but real agents err in their own ways. Log each identity's rare mistakes — a misread reef chart, a wrong deadline, an odd typo — and compare them across the population. When two identities commit the same rare error at the same hour, treat that coincidence as evidence of one operator and discount both. A farm must then run genuinely independent minds, paying the cost it tried to evade, or let every shared slip betray its clones.
